318076.title: The projectively independent configuration criterion for hierarchy adjacency
318076.statement:
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal C}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal D}$ be configurations of $k$ points in $\C^n$. Suppose that the projectivizations of the non-zero vectors in $\operatorname{\mathcal D}$ form a projectively independent set, hence of cardinality at most $n$. **Hierarchy conjecture.**

$$
Y_{\operatorname{\mathcal D}} \subset Y_{\operatorname{\mathcal C}}\qquad \Leftrightarrow \qquad \phi_{\operatorname{\mathcal D}}([Y_{\operatorname{\mathcal C}}])\not=0.
$$

This conjecture would characterize containment among the corresponding hierarchy strata using the restriction of the equivariant class. The authors report no counterexample when the stabilizer group of the configuration is larger than the trivial kernel case, but the criterion remains open in the stated projectively independent setting.
318076.source_name: L. M. Feher, A. Nemethi and R. Rimanyi, “Equivariant classes of matrix matroid varieties”, arXiv:0812.4871 (2008).
318076.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.4871

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

319227.title: Infinite log-concavity conjecture for Euler's difference-table sequences
319227.statement:
Let $d_n^k$ denote the entries of Euler's difference table, with $0\leq k\leq n$. For a sequence $\{a_k\}_{k\geq 0}$, define

$$
\mathfrak{L}\{a_k\}=\{a_k^2-a_{k-1}a_{k+1}\}.
$$

A sequence is **infinitely log-concave** when $\mathfrak{L}^l\{a_k\}$ is positive for every $l\geq 1$.

**Infinite log-concavity conjecture.** The sequence $\{d_n^k\}_{0\leq k\leq n}$ is infinitely log-concave.

The paper establishes ordinary log-concavity and motivates this stronger assertion with numerical evidence. Whether every sequence in Euler's difference table is infinitely log-concave remains open.
319227.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Cindy C. Y. Gu, Kevin J. Ma and Larry X. W. Wang, “Higher Order Log-Concavity in Euler's Difference Table”, arXiv:0911.2775 (2009).
319227.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.2775

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2009).

320997.title: Uniform lower-bound conjecture for critical-graph density constants
320997.statement:
For each integer $\ell\geq 3$, let $c_{\ell,k}$ be the quadratic-density constant for $k$-critical graphs of odd-girth at least $\ell$, with $k\geq 4$. **Uniform lower-bound conjecture.** For every fixed $\ell\geq 3$, the constants $c_{\ell,k}$ are bounded below by a constant independent of $k$:

$$
\inf_{k\geq 4} c_{\ell,k}>0.
$$

In particular, for each $\ell$ there should be a quadratic family of critical graphs of odd-girth $\ell$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
320997.source_name: Wesley Pegden, “Critical graphs without triangles: an optimum density construction”, arXiv:1101.4417 (2014).
320997.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4417

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

331339.title: The quasi-plane graph linear density conjecture
331339.statement:
Call a topological graph **$k$-quasi-plane** if it has no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. **The quasi-plane graph linear density conjecture.** For any integer $k \geq 2$ there is a constant $c_k$ such that every $n$-vertex $k$-quasi-plane graph has at most $c_kn$ edges.

This conjecture would imply the linear edge bound for PCC simple topological graphs. It is known for $k=3$, for $k=4$, and for convex geometric graphs for every $k$, but remains open for $k \geq 5$.
331339.source_name: Eyal Ackerman, Balázs Keszegh and Mate Vizer, “On the size of planarly connected crossing graphs”, arXiv:1509.02475 (2016).
331339.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.02475

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2015). “In Section we give a lower bound on the maximum size of a PCC simple topological graph, generalize the notion of planarly connected edges, and conclude with some open problems.”

333738.title: A majorization-product conjecture for bipartite graph degree and Laplacian data
333738.statement:
Let $n=p+q>1$ be an integer. Let $a\vdash p$ and $b\vdash q$ be integer partitions, and let $d=d_1\geq d_2\geq\dots\geq d_n$ be their union. Let $\lambda=\lambda_1\geq\dots\geq\lambda_{n-1}$ be a weakly decreasing sequence of positive real numbers. For partitions and sequences of equal total sum, write $\preceq$ for majorization, and let $b^*$ and $d^*$ denote conjugate partitions or conjugate degree sequences. **The majorization-product conjecture.** If

$$
a\preceq b^*\quad\text{and}\quad d\preceq\lambda\preceq d^*,
$$

then

$$
\frac{1}{n}\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i\leq\frac{1}{pq}\prod_{i=1}^n d_i.
$$

The inequality is motivated by the spanning-tree formula in terms of the Laplacian spectrum and by the Gale--Ryser theorem and Grone--Merris theorem, which constrain the possible degree sequences and spectra. The paper explicitly calls this conjecture incorrect, and Evan Chen provided a simple counterexample to a more general conjecture; therefore this statement is refuted.
333738.source_name: MLE Slone, “A conjectured bound on the spanning tree number of bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1608.01929 (2016).
333738.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.01929

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2016). “The author is grateful to Richard Ehrenborg, Kathryn Lybarger, Jack Schmidt, and Duane Skaggs for helpful conversations, and to Evan Chen for providing a simple counterexample to a more general conjecture.”

334469.title: Witness-tree probability conjecture for fully orderable witness trees
334469.statement:
A witness tree is built from bad-event labels, with children of a node labeled $B$ required to have distinct labels $B_1,\dots,B_s$ whose set is orderable to $B$. For a tree-structure $\tau$, let $P(\text{$\tau$ appears})$ denote the probability that it appears, and let $w(\tau)$ be the corresponding witness-tree weight. **Witness-tree lemma conjecture.** If this orderability condition is enforced at every node of $\tau$, then

$$
P(\text{$\tau$ appears})\leq w(\tau).
$$

The paper explains that this would strengthen the analysis of the Swapping Algorithm by controlling witness trees at every node rather than only at the root. Establishing the bound requires fine control over the temporal order of resamplings, which the authors were unable to maintain; the conjecture is presented as an open extension of their witness-tree lemma.
334469.source_name: David G. Harris, “New bounds for the Moser-Tardos distribution”, arXiv:1610.09653 (2019).
334469.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09653

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

339801.title: Bounded covering radius conjecture for lattices generated by unit vectors
339801.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a lattice generated by vectors of Euclidean norm $1$, and let $\rho_\infty(\mathcal{L})$ denote its covering radius with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm. **Unit-vector lattice covering-radius conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C$ such that

$$
\rho_\infty(\mathcal{L})\leq C
$$

for every lattice $\mathcal{L}$ generated by unit vectors.

This is presented as a weakening of the Komlós conjecture that could yield information about random matrices in the regime $n\gg m$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
339801.source_name: Cole Franks and Michael Saks, “On the Discrepancy of Random Matrices with Many Columns”, arXiv:1807.04318 (2018).
339801.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.04318

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2018). “This conjecture is still open.”

342147.title: The acyclic-matrix conjecture for dense zero-submatrices
342147.statement:
A zero-one matrix $P$ is **acyclic** if every submatrix of $P$ has a row or column containing at most one 1-entry. A matrix is **$P$-free** if it contains no submatrix equal to $P$.

**Acyclic-matrix conjecture.** For every acyclic zero-one matrix $P$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a $\delta>0$ such that every $P$-free $n\times n$ zero-one matrix with at least $\varepsilon n^2$ 0-entries contains a $\delta n\times\delta n$ all-0 submatrix.

This is presented as a strengthening of the simple-matrix conjecture. The proved results use the density of zero-entries to obtain large homogeneous submatrices in several special cases, but the asserted statement for arbitrary acyclic forbidden matrices remains open.
342147.source_name: Dániel Korándi, János Pach and István Tomon, “Large homogeneous submatrices”, arXiv:1903.06608 (2020).
342147.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06608

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

342273.title: The inverse-reward optimal strategy conjecture for booby trap search games
342273.statement: Consider a booby trap search game played on a hypergraph whose hyperedges $S$ have positive rewards $r(S)$. A Searcher strategy assigns probabilities $p(S)$ to choosing hyperedges. **Inverse-reward optimal strategy conjecture.** There exists an optimal Searcher strategy such that, for every hyperedge $S$, either $p(S)=0$ or $p(S)$ is inversely proportional to its reward $r(S)$; equivalently, the Searcher can attain optimality by choosing a suitable subset of hyperedges and using the mixed strategy described in Proposition~. This conjecture proposes a common form for optimal strategies suggested by the solutions of the special cases studied in the paper; whether it holds for every hypergraph is left open.
342273.source_name: Thomas Lidbetter and Kyle Lin, “A Search Game on a Hypergraph with Booby Traps”, arXiv:1903.12231 (2020).
342273.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.12231

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

342981.title: Euclidean algorithm quotient-sum conjecture
342981.statement:
For each integer $n\ge 2$, choose an integer $d$ with $1\le d\le n-1$ and $\gcd(n,d)=1$, and let $s(n,d)$ denote the sum of the quotients obtained by running the Euclidean algorithm on $(n,d)$. **Euclidean quotient-sum conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c$ such that, for every $n\ge 2$, some such $d$ satisfies

$$
s(n,d)\leq c\log n.
$$

The paper's preceding theorem gives the weaker bound $c\frac{n}{\phi(n)}\log n\log\log n$; removing the factor $\frac{n}{\phi(n)}\log\log n$ would be best possible in the stated scale and would yield stronger lower bounds for the first missing linear extension number.
342981.source_name: Noah Kravitz and Ashwin Sah, “Linear extension numbers of n-element posets”, arXiv:1906.06036 (2019).
342981.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

343312.title: Binary necklace-splitting conjecture for an arbitrary number of thieves
343312.statement:
A **necklace** consists of beads of $n$ kinds, and $r$ thieves are placed at the vertices of a cube of dimension $\lceil\log_2 r\rceil$, allowing some vertices to remain unoccupied. A **binary necklace splitting** is a fair splitting in which adjacent, possibly degenerate, pieces are allocated to thieves whose vertices share an edge. The size of a splitting is its number of cuts.

**Binary necklace-splitting conjecture.** Given a necklace with $n$ kinds of beads and $r\geq 4$ thieves, there exists a binary necklace splitting of size $(r-1)n$.

The conjecture was previously posed for arbitrary $r$; the paper proves it when $r$ is a power of two, via the binary necklace-splitting theorem, so the general case remains open in the source.
343312.source_name: Duško Jojić, Gaiane Panina and Rade Živaljević, “Splitting necklaces, with constraints”, arXiv:1907.09740 (2020).
343312.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1701.04955](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04955).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09740

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

350199.title: Worst-case variance conjecture for the chromatic number of random graphs
350199.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph with constant $p\in(0,1-1/e^2]$, let $Y_n=\chi(G_{n,p})$, and let $\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}(Y_n)$. Define

$$
w_n=\frac{\sqrt n\log\log n}{\log^3 n}.
$$

**Worst-case variance conjecture.** One has

$$
0<\limsup\frac{\sigma_n}{w_n}<\infty.
$$

Moreover, for every constant $c>0$ there is a constant $d>0$ such that, along every sequence of integers $n$ satisfying $\mu_{\alpha(n)}(n)\sim c n/\log^2 n$, one has $\sigma_n\sim d w_n$. This conjecture proposes that the polylogarithmic lower bound for the variance has the correct order in the worst case; the paper notes that one inequality is already implied by a theorem subject to an announced result.
350199.source_name: Annika Heckel and Oliver Riordan, “How does the chromatic number of a random graph vary?”, arXiv:2103.14014 (2023).
350199.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1903.08247](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.08247).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14014

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

351478.title: The critical-configuration conjecture for crown-free linear 3-graphs
351478.statement:
Let $C$ be the crown in a linear $3$-graph, consisting of three pairwise disjoint jewel edges and a base edge intersecting all three. For an edge $e=(a,b,c)$, let $D(e)=\langle d(a),d(b),d(c)\rangle$ be its degree vector, with coordinates in non-increasing order. A **critical configuration** is the set of $9$ edges incident to an edge $e$ satisfying

$$
D(e)=\langle 4,4,3\rangle\quad\text{or}\quad D(e)=\langle 5,4,2\rangle.
$$

A **minimal counterexample** is a crown-free linear $3$-graph violating ${\rm ex}(n,C)\leq\frac{3n}{2}$ with $n$ as small as possible.

**Critical-configuration conjecture.** Every minimal counterexample to

$$
{\rm ex}(n,C)\leq\frac{3n}{2}
$$

contains no critical configuration.

The conjecture is presented as a possible route to proving the almost-sharp upper bound ${\rm ex}(n,C)\leq\frac{3n}{2}$. The paper establishes that a crown-free linear $3$-graph with no critical configuration satisfies this bound, but does not prove that minimal counterexamples avoid such configurations.
351478.source_name: Alvaro Carbonero, Willem Fletcher, Jing Guo, András Gyárfás, Rona Wang and Shiyu Yan, “Crowns in linear 3-graphs”, arXiv:2107.14713 (2021).
351478.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14713

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

352093.title: Existence of an optimal data placement for arbitrary parameters
352093.statement:
Let $V$ be a set of $v$ servers, and let a data placement be a family of $b$ blocks, each of size $k$, on $V$. For a placement $(V,\mathcal{F})$, let

$$
P(\mathcal{F},x)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}v_jx^j,
$$

where $v_j$ is the number of ordered pairs of blocks intersecting in exactly $j$ elements and $x\geq1$. **Optimal data placement conjecture.** For any nonnegative integers $v$, $k$ and $b$, there exists an optimal data placement consisting of $b$ blocks of size $k$ on a $v$-set, meaning one that minimizes $P(\mathcal{F},x)$ for every $x\geq1$. The conjecture asserts simultaneous optimality for all failure probabilities; the paper studies this problem and, for triple replication, establishes existence in broad parameter ranges while leaving possible exceptional cases.
352093.source_name: Ruijing Liu and Junling Zhou, “Optimal data placements for triple replication”, arXiv:2109.14140 (2021).
352093.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14140

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

353242.title: Esperet's polylogarithmic induced-path conjecture for k-degenerate graphs
353242.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A graph is **$k$-degenerate** if every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $k$. For a graph with a path of order $n$, consider the order of its longest induced path.

**Esperet's conjecture.** There is a constant $d$ such that every $k$-degenerate graph that has a path of order $n$ also has an induced path of order at least

$$
(\log n)^d.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the polylogarithmic lower bound is the correct general bound for induced paths in $k$-degenerate graphs. It is posed as an open problem in the source; the paper proves such a bound for broader structural classes, but not for all $k$-degenerate graphs.
353242.source_name: Claire Hilaire and Jean-Florent Raymond, “Long induced paths in minor-closed graph classes and beyond”, arXiv:2201.03880 (2023).
353242.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.03880

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

354075.title: Characterisation of minimal hereditary graph classes of unbounded clique-width
354075.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}^\delta$ be the hereditary graph class associated with the sequence $\delta$, and let $\Delta_{min}$ denote the set of sequences satisfying the defining minimality conditions, including recurrence, bounded clique-width for gap factors, and bounded $\mathcal{M}^\beta$ for the bond set $\beta$.

**Characterisation conjecture.** The hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}^\delta$ is minimal of unbounded clique-width if and only if $\delta \in \Delta_{min}$.

The sufficient conditions for membership in $\Delta_{min}$ are known to yield minimal hereditary classes of unbounded clique-width, and recurrence together with bounded clique-width for gap factors is necessary. The unresolved part is whether the bond set must also have bounded $\mathcal{M}^\beta$; no counterexample with $\delta \notin \Delta_{min}$ is known.
354075.source_name: Robert Brignall and Daniel Cocks, “A framework for minimal hereditary classes of graphs of unbounded clique-width”, arXiv:2203.15446 (2023).
354075.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15446

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

365733.title: Kaneko's spanning-tree leaf-distance conjecture
365733.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$ be an integer and let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n\geq d+1$. For $S\subseteq V(G)$, let $i(G-S)$ denote the number of isolated vertices in $G-S$. **Kaneko's conjecture.** If

$$
i(G-S)<\frac{2|S|}{d-2}
$$

for every nonempty subset $S\subseteq V(G)$, then $G$ has a spanning tree with leaf distance at least $d$. The conjecture refines the known characterization for spanning trees of bounded leaf degree: decreasing the coefficient of $|S|$ in the condition is expected to force a larger leaf distance. The case of leaf distance at least three follows from existing results, while the general assertion is posed as an open conjecture.
365733.source_name: Jifu Lin and Lihua You, “The existence of a spanning tree with leaf distance at least d and leaf degree at most k via the size or the spectral radius with respect to the minimum degree”, arXiv:2411.06699 (2025).
365733.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06699

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

366444.title: Boesch's conjecture on uniformly most reliable graphs
366444.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$ be the set of all connected simple graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. For $G\in\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$, let $N_i^{(1)}(G)$ denote the number of spanning subgraphs of $G$ with $i$ edges and at most one connected component. A graph $G$ is a **0-element** in $\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$ if

$$
N_i^{(1)}(G)\geq N_i^{(1)}(H)
$$

for every $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$ and every $H\in\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$. A graph is **uniformly most reliable** if it is a $1$-uniformly most reliable graph, meaning that its reliability is at least that of every graph in $\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$ for every edge-retention probability $p\in[0,1]$.

**Boesch's conjecture.** Each uniformly most reliable graph in $\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$ is a $0$-element in $\mathcal{C}_{n,m}$.

Every $0$-element is uniformly most reliable, since its coefficientwise inequalities imply the corresponding reliability inequalities. The converse, proposed by Boesch in 1986, remains unresolved.
366444.source_name: Pablo Romero, “An algebraic characterization of strong graphs”, arXiv:2412.20702 (2024).
366444.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.20702

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2024). “The converse is an unresolved conjecture proposed in 1986 by Boesch .”

368500.title: Average number of realizable one-point extensions of planar chirotopes
368500.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, and choose uniformly at random a planar realizable chirotope $\chi$ of size $n$. For each realization of $\chi$, count the realizable one-point extensions, and average this count over all realizations of $\chi$. **Extension-counting conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that this average number of realizable one-point extensions is at most

$$
c\cdot n^4.
$$

The conjecture expresses the expectation that a typical realizable order type has its one-point extensions accessible from a common realization at the same polynomial scale as the upper bound for any fixed realization. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
368500.source_name: Xavier Goaoc and Arnau Padrol, “An asymptotic rigidity property from the realizability of chirotope extensions”, arXiv:2505.14189 (2025).
368500.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

371813.title: Polynomial growth and diffusive random walk for non-negatively curved graphs
371813.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $dgeq 1$, and suppose that $G$ has non-negative Ollivier--Ricci curvature and degrees bounded by $d$. Write $B(x,r)$ for the ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$, and let $X_n$ be the random walk started at $x$, with graph distance denoted by $d(X_0,X_n)$. **Polynomial-growth and diffusive-walk conjecture.** For each $d\geq 1$ there exists a constant $C_d$ such that

$$
\#B(x,r)\leq r^{C_d} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mathbf{E}_x\!\left[d(X_0,X_n)^2\right]\leq C_d n
$$

for every $n,r\geq 1$ and $x\in V$. This would strengthen the paper's subexponential-growth and near-diffusive estimates by giving polynomial growth of uniformly bounded dimension and a genuinely diffusive displacement bound, uniformly over the root vertex; the conjecture is presented as open.
371813.source_name: Tom Hutchcroft and Florentin Münch, “Bounded-degree graphs of non-negative Ollivier-Ricci curvature have subexponential growth and diffusive random walk”, arXiv:2512.03968 (2025).
371813.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03968

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).
